data.name: Asadul
data.gender_notes: Asadul is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Asadul is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'Asa', meaning 'Lord', and 'Dul', meaning 'of the Gods'. This name is a reverence to Lord Indra, the King of Gods, and is believed to bring strength, power, and divine blessings. The name Asadul carries the meaning “Lord of the Gods” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Asadul usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the gods and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embraces the divine power of the Lord.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Asadul total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

historical_references.reference: Asadul Khan was a prominent Bengali Muslim ruler during the late medieval period. He was the founder of the independent Bengal Sultanate in 1204 AD, marking the end of the Hindu Pala Empire in Bengal.
historical_references.context: End of the Hindu Pala Empire and founding of the independent Bengal Sultanate

historical_references.reference: Asadul Khan was also known as 'Raja Ganesha' during his reign in Bengal, and is believed to have adopted Hindu practices and even assumed a Hindu name, Ganesha, to strengthen his position among the Hindu population.
historical_references.context: Adoption of Hindu name and practices to strengthen political position

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Asadul' originates from Hindu mythology, specifically from the epic 'Mahabharata'. It is the name of a mighty warrior and a trusted advisor to the Pandava prince Bhima. In current times, the name 'Asadul' is gaining popularity, especially on social media platforms like Instagram, Twitter, and LinkedIn. Users often use the name as a unique handle or display name, reflecting a trend towards embracing cultural heritage and mythology. Some users may also use it as a sign of respect or connection to their Indian or Hindu roots. The Hindu mythology and folklore revival is a broader trend, as more people seek to connect with their cultural heritage and explore ancient Indian stories.
